description: GM bulletin 21-NA-108 (which superseded PIP5257E) covers engine overheating with the cooling system contaminated by engine oil, and it lists the 2020-2021 Cadillac XT6 with the 3.6L LGX V6 among the affected applications. The failure is not a head gasket in the usual sense: pressurized oil from the main oil gallery migrates into a coolant water jacket through porosity or a thin-wall casting defect in the engine block. Because oil pressure is far higher than coolant pressure, oil pushes into the coolant rather than the other way round, and the surge tank and radiator fill with a thick brown oil-and-coolant emulsion that looks like a milkshake. That emulsion will not carry heat, so the engine overheats, and it plugs the radiator and heater core. GM bulletins 21-NA-147 and 22-NA-240 cover the related diagnosis of a coolant and/or oil leak with the malfunction indicator lamp on. This is engine-code specific — it is an LGX 3.6L casting issue and is not a claim about the 2.0L LSY turbo four also sold in the XT6.
solution: Do not just flush the coolant and refill — the contamination will come straight back. Follow the bulletin's diagnostic sequence, which confirms the source by pressure-testing and by checking whether the oil level drops while the coolant turns to emulsion. Where the leak path is traced to block porosity, the repair is an engine block or complete engine replacement, which is why this is worth pursuing under the 6-year/70,000-mile GM powertrain warranty while it is still in force; document the concern in writing at the first sign of contamination. If contamination is confirmed, the radiator, surge tank, heater core and oil cooler all need flushing or replacement, since emulsified oil coats every passage. Out of warranty an engine replacement on an XT6 typically runs $8,000-$12,000.
note: 2020 XT6 Sport 3.6L LGX: replacement coolant is a companion supply AFTER repairing the oil-to-coolant leak and cleaning or replacing contaminated cooling components. It does not cure block porosity. This bottle is concentrate, not premix: the owner manual specifies a 50/50 mixture with clean, drinkable water. Follow the workshop refill procedure on a cool system. $19.85 per gallon of concentrate when reviewed September 6, 2026; confirm service quantity, tax and shipping.

description: GM PIP5608F covers 2020-2021 XT6 vehicles with 9-speed transmissions RPO M3G or M3W when torque-converter clutch shudder occurs on re-apply after a shift at 40 mph or below. GM identifies possible excessive assembly lubricant in the fluid and requires confirmation with TCC slip data or the scan-tool command test.
solution: Have a qualified transmission technician verify RPO M3G or M3W and confirm the event is TCC shudder using slip-speed data or the commanded-on test. If the bulletin criteria are met, follow the GM DEXRON VI drain-and-fill procedure and drive at least 200 miles before judging the repair. Do not use a universal additive or flush kit. The exact ShowMeTheParts lookup returned no transmission-fluid candidate.
note: 2020 XT6 Sport 3.6L: technician must confirm M3G/M3W and TCC shudder before the GM PIP5608F drain-and-fill repair. DEXRON-VI, not a universal additive or flush kit. Drive at least 200 miles before evaluating the repair. $6.96 shown per quart on September 6, 2026; seller defaults to quantity 12—confirm order pack and service quantity, tax and shipping.

description: The Power Transfer Unit (PTU) on AWD-equipped XT6 models develops seal leaks that allow fluid to seep out. Low PTU fluid causes the internal gears and bearings to wear prematurely, eventually producing a whining noise. The PTU is not included in routine maintenance schedules, so leaks often go unnoticed.
solution: Inspect the PTU seals and replace if leaking. Top off with the GM-specified PTU fluid. If the PTU is already noisy from running low on fluid, replacement is required as the unit is not rebuildable. Add PTU fluid level check to your routine maintenance schedule every 15,000 miles.
note: 2020 XT6 Sport 3.6L AWD power transfer unit only; confirm VIN and unit with seller. GM 19352759 / ACDelco 10-4108 DEXRON 75W-90 is not automatic-transmission fluid or rear-clutch fluid. Repair the leaking seal before restoring fluid level; a noisy, damaged unit needs professional diagnosis, not just a top-off. $21.47 per 32-oz bottle when reviewed September 6, 2026; confirm service quantity, tax and shipping.
